I couldn't find any source that mentions `fetchMock` by name in connection with this package. The search results do show that the package was renamed and that its outbound-request mocking moved to MSW.

**The rename:** Cloudflare's package is now `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin`, and the older name was `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` ([changelog](https://docs-durable-objects-instance-replaced-errors.previews.developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-08-19-vitest-plugin/)). A codemod can update the dependency, imports, and TypeScript config. The Vitest configuration API itself is unchanged ([migration guide](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/migration-guides/migrate-to-vitest-plugin/)).

**Mocking now uses MSW:** Cloudflare's current docs direct you to `@msw/cloudflare` for mocking outbound HTTP and WebSocket requests. They say to install MSW 2.14 or later, using `npm i -D msw@^2.14.0 @msw/cloudflare`. The setup creates a network mock with `setupNetwork()` and calls `enable()`, `resetHandlers()`, and `disable()` from Vitest hooks ([Cloudflare docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/mock-outbound-requests/)).

**Removal of the old mocking:** A third-party write-up says outbound request mocking was removed from the package and replaced by `msw` and `@msw/cloudflare` ([eCorpIT](https://ecorpit.com/cloudflare-vitest-plugin-1-0-msw-peer-dependency-conflict-2026/)). That article also flags a peer-dependency mismatch between the two packages. I couldn't confirm that claim against Cloudflare or npm, so check it before relying on it.

**Gaps:**
- I found no official changelog entry that lists `fetchMock` as a removed API.
- The `fetchMock` name appears in unrelated third-party packages (`fetch-mock`, `@fetch-mock/vitest`, `vitest-fetch-mock`), which may be what you're thinking of.

To confirm, check the package's release notes on GitHub (cloudflare/workers-sdk) for the 1.0.0 release, or search that repo's changelog for `fetchMock`.

input.prompt: What exactly is the peer dependency conflict between msw and @msw/cloudflare, which versions, and the fix?

toolu_01L9zMRgaYXVJnTAVFYSamzs.prompt: What exactly is the peer dependency conflict between msw and @msw/cloudflare, which versions, and the fix?

content.content:
The conflict is a version mismatch between Cloudflare's install command and the peer range that `@msw/cloudflare` declares:

- **Cloudflare's documented command** installs `msw@^2.14.0`. The caret range permits msw 2.14.0.
- **`@msw/cloudflare` 0.0.1** declares a peer dependency on msw `>=2.14.1`.
- **The conflict:** msw 2.14.0 satisfies Cloudflare's instruction but fails the package's own peer requirement.

Most lockfile-free installs will resolve msw 2.15.0 (published 8 July 2026), so no warning appears. A pinned or resolution-constrained monorepo that lands on 2.14.0 will get a peer warning, or an install failure under strict pnpm settings.

**Fix:** install `msw@^2.14.1` instead of `msw@^2.14.0`. The article also recommends pinning `@msw/cloudflare` to an exact version, since it is a 0.0.1 package with no declared licence and no releases.

content.text:
Yes. MSW is now Cloudflare's official way to mock outbound requests in Workers Vitest tests. But the install command in Cloudflare's docs no longer works with the latest `@msw/cloudflare`, so the version you need depends on which `@msw/cloudflare` you install.

**Background:** In August 2026, `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` was renamed to `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin`. A codemod updates the dependency, imports and TS config, and the Vitest config API is the same. According to a third-party write-up (I didn't confirm this in an official changelog), the built-in outbound mocking was removed at the same time in favor of `msw` plus `@msw/cloudflare`.

**Versions:**
- Cloudflare's docs say to run `npm i -D msw@^2.14.0 @msw/cloudflare`.
- The npm registry today shows:
  - `@msw/cloudflare` 0.0.x and 0.1.0 require `msw >=2.14.1`. That's slightly stricter than the docs, so msw 2.14.0 triggers a peer warning, or a failure under strict pnpm.
  - `@msw/cloudflare` 0.2.0, the current `latest` (published 2026-09-28), requires `msw >=3`.
  - The current `msw` latest is 3.0.2.

The docs' command pins msw to 2.x while pulling the newest `@msw/cloudflare`, so the two will conflict. Install a matching pair instead:

```sh
# Current pairing (recommended)
npm i -D msw@^3 @msw/cloudflare@^0.2.0

# Or, if you need to stay on MSW 2.x
npm i -D msw@^2.14.1 @msw/cloudflare@0.1.0
```

`@msw/cloudflare` is still 0.x, so pin it to an exact version or check the changelog before you upgrade. I haven't checked whether the 0.2.0 / MSW 3 setup still matches the docs example below, which was written for MSW 2.14.

**Setup (from Cloudflare's docs):**

```ts
// test/network.ts
import { setupNetwork } from "@msw/cloudflare";
export const network = setupNetwork();
```

```ts
// test/setup.ts  (add to `setupFiles` in your Vitest config)
import { afterAll, afterEach, beforeAll } from "vitest";
import { network } from "./network";

beforeAll(() => network.enable());
afterEach(() => network.resetHandlers());
afterAll(() => network.disable());
```

This covers both outbound HTTP and WebSocket requests.

Ludion had no lessons on this. The version details come from the npm registry and Cloudflare's docs.

Sources:
- [Cloudflare docs – Mock outbound requests](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/mock-outbound-requests/)
- [Cloudflare – Migrate to @cloudflare/vitest-plugin](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/migration-guides/migrate-to-vitest-plugin/)
- [Changelog: vitest-pool-workers is now vitest-plugin](https://docs-durable-objects-instance-replaced-errors.previews.developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-08-19-vitest-plugin/)
- [eCorpIT – vitest-plugin 1.0 MSW peer dependency conflict](https://ecorpit.com/cloudflare-vitest-plugin-1-0-msw-peer-dependency-conflict-2026/)
- [npm registry – @msw/cloudflare](https://registry.npmjs.org/@msw/cloudflare)
- [npm registry – msw](https://registry.npmjs.org/msw)
